column1: # HISTORICAL SPLIT SOURCE — NOT CONSUMED BY THE CURRENT BUILD. Edit `script/en.tsv` and
# follow `TRANSLATING.md` / `VWF_BUDGETS.md`. Comments below preserve early POC decisions
# and may mention superseded fixed-cell limits; they are not translator instructions.
# KEY IS `loc` (bank:$addr), never the sequential id: ids are reassigned by sorted
# offset, so any change to extraction silently shifts an id-keyed file by one entry.
# Length: these are almost all table-referenced, so storage is not the limit — the tool
# relocates them. The real limit is DISPLAY WIDTH, and each menu box is sized to its
# widest entry. Budgets used here (cells, including the cursor space the tool prepends):
# STALE COMMENT REMOVED 2026-08-04: this said "the box is 4 cells wide, everything here is
# therefore <= 4", which was measured on the JAPANESE box and stopped being true when
# script/box_geometry.tsv widened boxes 6/39 from x=13,w=5 to x=9,w=9. The budget is
# 8 CELLS, not 4 -- byte 0 is the cursor. That is what let the action labels expand to
# Eat/Equip/Remove. FINDINGS.md predicted exactly this: the box is
# right-aligned with slack to its left, and the item list beside it ends at column 10.
# Recovered 2026-07-29: the pointer table was being read as 15 entries, so these three were
# invisible. They are LIVE -- ひろう and だす come from the category tables at 30:$7E14 and
# $7E40, はずす from the equip/remove substitution at 30:$7D73.
# One line per BOX ROW. The rows of a box are one allocation, so a box that anything
# points at can grow; box 2 is pinned (see script.json `box.pinned`) and each of its rows
# is limited to its original cell count.
# These addresses used to be a byte-count guess away from the truth: 31:$41E2 and
# 31:$4414 were the DESCRIPTOR of the box below them, and the translation had to carry
# six or eight <$XX> layout bytes to step over it. Now that box_descriptors() finds the
# real row starts, the descriptor is data again and the text begins where it says.
# 31:$41F6 is a composite: two labels sharing one row, split by the vertical bar glyph
# $B6. The <$B6> token emits that byte verbatim so the column layout survives.
# Box 1 is 11 cells and the VALUE is drawn right-aligned on the row BELOW its label
# (screenshot: "Gld" then "0G" beneath it), so the label has all 11 cells to itself.
# There was no reason for three-letter abbreviations here.
# なんいど = 難易度, "difficulty level". The game calls its difficulty choices dungeon
# paths elsewhere, so "Path" is both compact and consistent with that terminology.
# The tool prepends the cursor space itself where the original row starts with one, so
# these are one cell narrower than the box. "Normal" needs a 7-wide box; the cursor follows
# the box now, so it fits.
# One line per box ROW. Budgets come from two places and both are checked:
#   - the box `width` (box_geometry.tsv overrides it) -- how much the drawer will draw
#   - for a PINNED box, the original cell count -- pinned rows cannot grow, because a
#     second reader points into the middle of the block and relocating it would leave
#     that pointer stale. `pinned` is in script.json under each row's `box`.
# ---- inventory titles (each its own one-row box) ----
# ---- item categories: box 33 consumables, box 34 equipment ----
# HELD BACK -- these do not fit, and not for want of total space. Bank 31's descriptors sit
# between the text blocks, so its free pool is a set of runs of at most 26 bytes, and these
# two boxes need 32 and 38 contiguous. build.py reports it as fragmentation, not shortfall.
# The 116 contiguous bytes of the katakana grid page are what unlocks them; see HANDOFF.md.
# Uncomment together with a width of 7 for both boxes in box_geometry.tsv.
# ---- messages. 18 cells, and the leading space is re-added for you ----
# Kept short on purpose: bank 31's pool is 534 bytes and these all draw from it. The
# 116 bytes of the katakana grid page are the obvious place to get more (task 4).
# ---- title screen: start menu, rankings, dungeon entrances ----
# "Kuyou Pass" would make this box 26 bytes, and the only 26-byte run in bank 31 is the
# one box 33 needs. 26+24 into 26+23 does not fit however it is ordered.
# ---- difficulty explanations (boxes 46/48/50, all PINNED: budget is the original) ----
# Row 2 of each is centred by hand in the original; one leading space is re-added, the
# rest is up to the text.
# Box 48 is NOT translatable in place. Row 1 is 20 bytes but only 16 cells -- four
# dakuten -- and English has none, so nothing can consume 20 bytes inside an 18-cell box
# without pushing row 2 two bytes early. build.py rejects it; translating row 2 alone
# would leave the box half-Japanese, so both stay.
# ---- name-entry page label + menu words (boxes 12 and 13, row 0) ----
# The three words are SELECTABLE, and the picker maps cursor positions to columns, so
# these keep the original column layout exactly: label at 0-3, then 6-8, 10-12, 15-17.
# Moving them would move what the cursor lands on.
# Box 13 -- the second page -- is now ALIASED to box 12 in script/box_alias.tsv, so it has
# no rows of its own to translate and this key would match no string. Its 116 bytes are
# what let the item category boxes keep "Staff". The visible toggle action is retired;
# both internal page branches resolve to box 12. This legacy staging file is not consumed
# by build.sh, but these rows mirror canonical script/en.tsv for reference.
# Ten real composer lines, chosen from a `msglog.py` transcript so every one is text the
# game demonstrably draws, and covering the three shapes the sample had to cover:
# combat fragments with runtime substitutions, a speaker-prefixed village line, and one
# long multi-box conversation. Their purpose is to answer whether fixed-width English at
# 18 cells reads badly -- see HANDOFF.md TASK 2.

# Control codes are written by NAME (``, `
`, ``), the same tokens
# codec.decode prints in script.tsv's `jp` column. Do NOT spell them `<$E2>`: an escape
# means "layout byte, reserve it out of the DTE code space", and a control code is
# ---- combat fragments (bank 13, relocatable, and already DTE-allowlisted) ----
# These are FRAGMENTS assembled at render time, not sentences: `<var>` pulls a name from
# the message queue and `<cE4>` a number, so each pair below draws as two lines of one
# box. Japanese orders them "X wa Y ni / dealt <cE4> points of damage"; English keeps the
# same split, with the verb on line 1 and the number on line 2, so no fragment boundary
# The widths quoted are the LITERAL cells. A `<var>` costs whatever the substituted name
# costs, and monster names are still Japanese, so the real width of these lines is not
# knowable until item and monster names are translated.
# "Dodged <var>!" rather than "Dodged <var>'s attack!" -- the latter is 22 literal cells
# before the name is substituted, so it could not fit the 18-cell line under ANY name.
# 11 literal cells, so this one tolerates a name of 7. "<var> reached level <cE4>!" would
# have been 20 literal cells and could never fit.
# ---- hunger warnings (bank 13; the last two are IN-PLACE and byte-capped) ----
# $45DF has 19 bytes and $45F3 has 16, and neither is DTE-allowlisted, so those two are
# hard byte limits with no compression to spend. "About to collapse!" is 20 bytes with
# the <cE0:88> prefix and does not fit; "Ready to drop!" does.
# ---- village dialogue (bank 14, ALL in-place: the pointer is computed at runtime, so
# these cannot be repointed and must fit their original byte count exactly) ----
# The speaker prefix is where the budget goes. `おかみ「` is 4 bytes; `Innkeeper: ` is 11.
# The font has no `"` glyph (available punctuation is  !'()+,-./:?[]~ ), so attribution
# is `Name: ` with no quotes -- which is also 2 bytes cheaper than 「...」 would have been.
